newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Don't get over excited over NZ CPI data says Birch.
newsitem.headline: Don't get over excited over NZ CPI data says Birch.

text.p: Finance Minister Bill Birch on Tuesday warned people not to get over excited about a single set of lower-than-expected inflation data.
He said the data would improve confidence in the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's ability to hit its inflation target over the next 12 months.

The debt market rallied strongly after CPI inflation in the September year came out at 2.4 percent against market expectations of 2.7 percent and the RB's estimate of underlying inflation came out at 2.34 percent against its own forecast of 2.7 percent and the market's forecast of 2.6 percent.

"The quarterly result is consistent with the Reserve Bank's price stability target of 0 to 2 percent and will improve public confidence in the ability of the bank to achieve that target in the next 12 months," Birch said.
"However, at this stage, underlying inflation still remains above the target band. I don't want to get over-excited about any single result. What matters is maintaining progress over time."
Birch said price stability was the goal.
"By achieving and maintaining it, the bank makes its best contribution to sustained economic growth," he said.
